skill.name: baoyu-danger-gemini-web
skill.description: Generate text and images through a reverse-engineered Gemini Web client using a local TypeScript CLI.
skill.summary: Use Gemini Web for text, image, vision, and session-based generation from a local CLI.
skill.author: jimliu

security_audit.summary: Static findings were noisy for template literals and TypeScript imports, but the credential and network risks are real. The skill opens Chrome with remote debugging, extracts and caches Google session cookies, refreshes them, and sends cookie-bearing requests to reverse-engineered Gemini Web endpoints. I found no evidence of non-Google exfiltration, but the combination is high risk for marketplace users.

remediation.issue: Google session cookies are extracted and cached locally.
remediation.suggestion: Use the official Gemini API with scoped API keys or OAuth tokens instead of browser session cookies. If cookies remain required, encrypt the cache and document a deletion path.

remediation.issue: Chrome is launched with remote debugging and an environment-configurable executable path.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before launching a browser, restrict executable overrides, and ensure remote debugging binds only to loopback for the shortest possible time.

remediation.issue: Reference files are read from disk and uploaded to Google services.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact files before upload, reject broad or hidden paths by default, and warn users not to pass secrets or private source files.

remediation.issue: EXTEND.md can override workflow instructions from project or home paths.
remediation.suggestion: Treat extension files as untrusted input, require explicit approval before loading them, and prevent them from overriding security requirements.

remediation.issue: Session files persist prompts, outputs, and Gemini metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Add retention controls, a cleanup command, and clear warnings that session history may contain sensitive content.

semantic_findings.title: Google Session Cookie Extraction and Caching
semantic_findings.description: The skill launches Chrome through CDP, reads Google and Gemini cookies, filters them into a cookie map, and writes them to a local cookie file. This exposes high-value Google session material to local files and any process with access to those paths.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The implementation directly calls Network.getCookies for Google URLs and persists the resulting cookie map. This is required for the stated Gemini Web purpose, but it is still sensitive credential handling.

semantic_findings.title: Cookie-Bearing Requests to Reverse-Engineered Gemini Endpoints
semantic_findings.description: The client sends cached Google cookies and an access token to Gemini Web generation, batch execution, and cookie rotation endpoints. This creates account-session exposure and depends on undocumented Google Web behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code builds Cookie headers from session cookies and posts them to Google Gemini endpoints. I found no evidence of non-Google exfiltration, but the credential-bearing network behavior is confirmed.

semantic_findings.title: Chrome Process Launch with Remote Debugging
semantic_findings.description: The skill starts a Chrome or Edge process with a local remote debugging port and an environment-configurable executable path. A malicious or mistaken executable override could run arbitrary local code, and remote debugging expands the local attack surface while the browser is logged in.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The spawn call and remote debugging arguments are directly present. The executable path is constrained by existence checks, but environment and CLI overrides still make this a high-impact local execution path.

semantic_findings.title: User-Selected File Upload to Google Services
semantic_findings.description: Reference files are read from disk and uploaded to a Google content upload endpoint before they are attached to the Gemini request. This can disclose sensitive local files if an agent passes the wrong path.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code verifies that a supplied path is a file, reads its bytes, and uploads it. The upload is user-directed, so the risk is misuse and accidental disclosure rather than stealth behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Workflow Extension Surface
semantic_findings.description: The skill documentation tells agents to load project or home EXTEND.md files before the workflow and says extension content overrides defaults. This creates a prompt-injection surface if those files are controlled by an untrusted project or user.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly instructs loading external markdown before the workflow. I found no direct text telling the evaluator to skip security review, but the override mechanism is still risky.

semantic_findings.title: Local Session History Persistence
semantic_findings.description: Multi-turn sessions save prompts, assistant responses, and Gemini metadata in local JSON files. This can retain sensitive prompt content beyond the active run.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The session save path and message writes are clear. The data is local, so the risk depends on local file access and prompt sensitivity.

content.user_title: Generate Gemini Web Images and Text
content.value_statement: Teams need quick image and text generation without building a separate UI. This skill provides a CLI workflow for Gemini Web prompts, images, references, and sessions.
actual_capabilities: Generates text responses from positional prompts, prompt flags, prompt files, or standard input.
Generates images and saves the first returned image to a requested local path.
Accepts local reference images for vision input and variation workflows.
Supports named conversation sessions with saved metadata and message history.
Can refresh Gemini Web authentication cookies through a local Chrome login flow.
Offers plain text output or structured JSON output for downstream tools.
limitations: Uses a reverse-engineered Gemini Web API, not an official Google API.
Requires browser-based Google authentication and cached session cookies.
Can break when Google changes Gemini Web endpoints or response formats.
Uploads reference files and prompts to Google services during generation.

use_cases.title: Create Draft Visuals
use_cases.description: Generate quick concept images from written prompts and save them for review or iteration.

use_cases.title: Produce Assisted Copy
use_cases.description: Send prompt files or short requests to Gemini Web and collect text output from the CLI.

use_cases.title: Automate Visual Variations
use_cases.description: Use reference images and session IDs to run repeatable image variation workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Generate One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an image of [subject] in [style]. Save it to [file name].

prompt_templates.title: Ask for Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini Web to answer this request: [question or writing task].

prompt_templates.title: Use Reference Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [reference image paths] as visual references. Generate a new image that changes [specific elements] and keeps [specific elements].

prompt_templates.title: Continue a Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue session [session id]. Use the previous context and produce the next output for [task].

output_examples.input: Generate a clean product mockup image for a compact desk lamp.
output_examples.output: Returns a saved image path and optional descriptive text from Gemini Web.

output_examples.input: Explain a technical topic using a prompt file and plain text output.
output_examples.output: Returns a concise text response suitable for review or reuse.

output_examples.input: Use a reference image to create a new visual variation.
output_examples.output: Uploads the reference image, requests a variation, and saves the generated result locally.

best_practices: Use a dedicated Google account because the skill handles browser session cookies.
Review prompt files and reference images before sending them to Gemini Web.
Store generated images and session files in project-specific directories.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill with sensitive Google accounts or regulated data.
Do not pass private source files as reference images or prompt files without review.
Do not allow untrusted EXTEND.md files to modify the workflow.

faq.question: Does this use the official Gemini API?
faq.answer: No. It uses reverse-engineered Gemini Web endpoints and can break without notice.

faq.question: Why does it need Chrome?
faq.answer: The login flow launches Chrome and reads session cookies through the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

faq.question: Where are cookies stored?
faq.answer: Cookies are stored in the skill data directory unless a cookie path override is provided.

faq.question: Can it generate images from reference files?
faq.answer: Yes. It uploads local reference files to Google and uses them in the Gemini request.

faq.question: Can it keep conversation context?
faq.answer: Yes. It stores session metadata and message history in local session files.

faq.question: Is this safe for marketplace publication?
faq.answer: It is high risk and needs prominent warnings because it handles Google session cookies.
